title: Correlation estimates change sign after a one-pulse shift in 106 of 255 Allen mouse V1 connections
abstract: We tested how pulse position affects correlation estimates in selected Allen mouse V1 slice connections. Trial fits reproduced 267 of 268 finite stored first-pair correlations within 1e-10. One inspected public source revision instead reproduced the later pair in all 267 cases with sufficient fits. The exact release build is unknown. On identical three-pulse trials from 255 connections and 82 inferred mice, the first and later pair estimates had opposite signs in 106 connections. The donor-weighted mean difference was -0.04337, with a nominal 95 percent interval of -0.07913 to -0.00637. The excitatory subgroup interval included zero. Most connections had about 25 trials. Only two opposite-sign pairs had both nominal Fisher intervals exclude zero. Thus, sign changes in sample estimates are not secure biological classifications. The result supports a trial-based pulse-position check before summary comparisons. It does not identify a defect in the stored correlation field, a release mechanism, or a rule across regions and species. We provide code, sufficient statistics, source hashes, replay checks, and retrieval instructions.
